title: Evidence capture failover & ephemeral proofing playbook
body:
Purpose
------
This playbook documents an operational approach for collectors to tolerate transient failures, buffer evidence ephemerally with verifiable integrity, export to downstream SIEMs under backpressure, and perform controlled rollbacks/replays during incident response. Goal: keep production services non-blocking while ensuring every relevant control artifact can be proven, replayed, or forensically reconstructed if asked by audit/compliance.

Intended audience
-----------------
- Security engineers implementing collectors
- SREs operating ingest pipelines
- Compliance engineers responsible for evidence retention and proofing
- Solutions engineers integrating SIEM exports for customers

Non-goals
---------
- This is not a full schema spec for the audit payload. See linked Evidence Envelope Spec for fields.
- This playbook does not replace long-term cold storage policies. It focuses on edge/near-edge buffering and failover behavior.

Key concepts / definitions
-------------------------
- Ephemeral buffer: short-lived, local storage on collector host (or sidecar) used to persist evidence while downstream connectivity is degraded. TTL <= 72h by default.
- Proof packet: compact cryptographic summary attached to an evidence chunk (SHA256 + sequence number + signer id). Enables later chain-of-custody verification without storing entire secondary artifacts.
- Export window: configured time range (e.g., 00:00-04:00 local) where bulk export/replay is allowed to reduce daytime burst. Configurable per-customer.
- Backpressure mode: state where collector reduces sampling, aggregates events, or routes lower-priority evidence to low-cost channels.

Design principles
-----------------
1) Non-blocking on the request path: collectors must not add end-user latency. Evidence capture should be asynchronous by default.
2) Boundaries on local storage: ephemeral buffer capacity must be limited and enforced with eviction policies and TTLs.
3) Verifiability: every stored chunk must have a proof packet enabling later integrity checks.
4) Graceful degradation: when SIEM/export endpoints are unreachable, collectors must transition through graded modes (retry -> aggregate -> degrade -> failover) with clear operator-triggered and automated paths.
5) Safe replay: replays must be idempotent and tagged with a replay_id and original_timestamp to avoid double-counting in downstream systems.

Collector state machine (high-level)
-----------------------------------
- NORMAL: healthy connectivity and export. Evidence exported in real time.
- RETRYING: transient failures (HTTP 5xx, network flaps). Exponential backoff with jitter; buffer writes continue.
- AGGREGATING: sustained degradation; collector switches to batch/summary exports (compact events, counts) for low-priority streams.
- DEGRADED: capacity thresholds exceeded or SIEM unreachable; low-priority evidence evicted earliest, high-priority retained with proof packets. Operator alert.
- FAILOVER: configured fallback exporter (secondary SIEM, S3 bucket, or partner log-archive) receives export.
- REPLAY: triggered manually or by automated job to flush ephemeral buffers to canonical store.

Buffering and TTL policy guidance
---------------------------------
- Default ephemeral buffer size: 10 GB per collector host. Tunable via config per tier.
- Default TTL: 72 hours. Shorter TTL (24h) for high-volume tenants.
- Eviction order: tombstones/metadata for low-priority audit events -> aggregations (counts) -> raw events for low-priority sources -> raw events for medium priority -> retain high-priority (auth, privileged actions) until TTL or space reclaimed.
- Emergency retention: operator can elevate TTL to 7 days for a tenant during incident; this must create an auditable change record (who, why, window).

Proof packet format (summary)
---------------------------
- sequence_id: string (monotonic per-collector)
- chunk_hash: sha256 hex of chunk payload
- signer_id: collector instance id
- signed_blob: ed25519 signature over (sequence_id || chunk_hash || timestamp || signer_id)
Notes: store proof packets alongside files in local buffer index. Proof packets are intentionally compact so they can be exported even when bandwidth is constrained. Full format in Evidence Envelope Spec.

Export/backpressure strategies
------------------------------
1) Priority-based routing: tag events with priority levels (P0 privileged config change, P1 auth events, P2 system telemetry, P3 app custom logs). Only P0/P1 retained in DEGRADED.
2) Adaptive batching: when export rate limit triggered, aggregate sequential similar events into an "aggregate chunk" containing N events and a combined proof. Downstream consumers must accept aggregated forms.
3) Progressive backoff with fallback: after N retries over M minutes, switch to secondary exporter. Secondary exporters must be treated as write-once archives and be immutable.
4) Sampling as last resort: if disk and all failovers are exhausted, sample low-priority streams at configurable ratio (default 1%). Sampling must be logged in audit trail and reversible for replay if stored samples are insufficient.

Operational runbook (for on-call)
---------------------------------
Immediate detection (automated)
- Alert: collector-export-failure (>= 5m) fires.
- Pager: oncall-sec (P1)
- Dashboard checks: buffer utilization, oldest-event-age, outbound 5xx rate.

Triage steps
1) Verify alert: check collector logs for exporter error codes. Identify affected tenants and priority classes.
2) Check network: attempt curl from collector to exporter endpoint via purple team proxy.
3) Toggle to FAILOVER: if primary is down > 10m, instruct system to execute automated failover to preconfigured S3 sink.
4) Confirm proof export: ensure proof packets for the last 24h are present in failover sink.
5) Run replay job: once primary is back, schedule controlled replay in the Export Window. Attach replay_id and comment in audit record.

Rollback / replay considerations
- All replays must include replay_id and replay_offset to allow downstream deduplication.
- Downstream consumers must be able to accept an idempotency key; when missing, system should rely on time-window heuristics.
- Replay concurrency: limit to 2 parallel replays per downstream endpoint to avoid flooding.

Forensics and verification steps (post-incident)
------------------------------------------------
1) Verify chain-of-custody: validate proof packets against signing keys stored in KMS/HSM.
2) Reconstruct timeline: use sequence_ids and timestamps from proof packets to build authoritative ordering.
3) Hash reconciliation: compare chunk_hash values with hashes stored in canonical store after replay.
4) Incident write-up: include the TTL override record, failover activation time, replay_id, and any sampled volumes or evicted artifacts.

Testing and chaos experiments (SRE/Eng playbook)
------------------------------------------------
- Purpose-built chaos tests:
  - Simulate exporter 503 for 30m and assert collector transitions: NORMAL -> RETRYING -> AGGREGATING -> FAILOVER.
  - Disk pressure test: fill ephemeral buffer to 95% and assert eviction order and alerting.
  - Signing key rotation: rotate collector signer keys and assert proof packets are still verifiable with key history.
- Metrics to track in experiments: export_success_rate, buffer_utilization, oldest_event_age, proof_export_rate, replay_success_rate.

Config knobs (operator-facing)
-------------------------------
- ephemeral_buffer_capacity (bytes)
- ephemeral_ttl_hours
- priority_threshold_for_eviction
- failover_target_uri
- retry_policy (base_ms, max_attempts, jitter)
- export_window_cron
- sampling_ratio_for_low_priority

Open questions / decisions to make (TODOs)
-----------------------------------------
- Should proof packets include a lightweight NVME attestation for on-host tamper evidence? Pros/cons need legal review.
- How to model multi-tenant eviction fairness under disk pressure? Round-robin or weighted by tenant priority?
- Downstream aggregated chunk schema needs to be standardized across SIEM partners. Action: product to own compatibility contract.

References & links
------------------
- Evidence Envelope Spec (linked)
- JIRA-SEC-1187: "Collector ephemeral buffer implementation"
- CON-4122: retention exceptions process

Appendix: minimal playbook checklist for SRE when primary SIEM unreachable
------------------------------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Identify affected collectors and tenants (script: tools/identify-affected.sh)
- [ ] Confirm proof packet presence in local index for last 48h
- [ ] Enable failover target and verify write success to secondary sink
- [ ] Open ticket and tag compliance (compliance@redwood.ai)
- [ ] Schedule replay in export window and add owner, replay_id, and expected duration to ticket

Notes to self (author)
---------------------
- Need to sync with solutions engineering to confirm partner SIEMs accept aggregated chunks.
- Add example curl commands for failover write verification.
- Convert this doc into an operations runbook with runbook-run links once validated.
